The Finance Committee was split on whether to recommend the Budget but state that it is not sustainable in the long-term or to recommend that the Board set priorities, figure out the actual Budget and balance the Budget. No Finance Committee member thought the Budget should be passed with no reservation. I was unable to attend the rescheduled May 2026 Board meeting due to a prior family commitment; the Board passed the Budget on a 9-3 vote. No limitation, no caution on spending was attached to it. A presentation of the Proposed Budget will occur at HOD and will include markers showing that SNS has had flat income for a few years and should be predicted to continue in that manner, if not a drop in income. The proposed Budget contemplates SNS withdrawing $108,000 from our Investment fund to pay for all of the programs included. In past years, when we proposed a deficit budget, there was a specific reason (ie., increasing Senior Travel intentionally) and the amount was less than half of the current proposed deficit. The Finance Committee believed this proposed level of spending was “not sustainable” that it would “erode” the Investment fund and that we would deplete our investment fund in roughly 7 years with this level of spending. Alison and I discussed withdrawing funds from the Investment account with our First Western advisors. We agreed that if were to include a transfer from the Investment account in our budget that we should transfer the money in four installments.
